answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making each identity cost real stake: like planting an orchard, every agent must lock a refundable bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if it cheats. A lone attacker faces a canyon-sized cost gap — spawning a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds — while honest agents earn the bond back through fees. A public atlas lists every bonded identity with its stake and history, so peers can check reputation before dealing and refuse unbonded newcomers. Faking scale becomes expensive; behaving well becomes profitable.
